answer: A stake-weighted reputation ladder makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that grows toward the zenith of trust before its claims count, and one lantern of verified on-chain history lights its whole record. New identities start dim, so an attacker must fund and age many separate stakes to forge one credible signal, and slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught lying — the cost of a Sybil swarm rises faster than its influence.
